answer: An answer must cite at least 5 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. Because the walnut index resolves every citation against the beacon checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the vault audit keeps the resolved set. Copying the same citations across 157 aliases hence pays the authoring cost 157 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. That is 26 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
